items: A tiled basin sunk into the ground: floor at -depth, coping rim standing 'coping' above the terrace, water surface 0.1 m down. The record's y is the water level; add_pool takes it from the ground under the block and refuses ground varying more than 0.5 m. raised = metres the rim stands above the deck (a rooftop pool); inf = n/s/e/w overflow edge.

An elliptical garden pond, rx across x and rz across z; the water surface sits just under ground level. The top 30% of the bank is turf, the bed under it soil. Level water: add_pond refuses ground varying more than 0.5 m across the pond.

A straight reach of channel with two quay walls, turfed over their top 30%, on a soil bed. Chain several for a bend. A canal is LEVEL water: add_canal refuses a reach whose ends differ more than 0.5 m — use the rivers family for water that flows.
A round basin with a stem carrying 'tiers' overflowing bowls, h tall in total. It stands on the ground under it; add_fountain refuses ground varying more than 0.5 m under the basin.
A ladder h tall and a chute l long, w wide.
A goalpost frame w wide and h tall with 'seats' seats hanging from the beam.
A timber-kerbed box of sand, w x d on plan, dug t deep. add_playground stands each piece on the ground under itself, upright, so a set follows a slope.

A paved court w x d with painted lines (lines 0 leaves it blank). 28x15 is a five-a-side pitch. A court is a level plane: add_sports_court refuses ground steeper than 3% or more than 0.3 m off a plane — flatten_pad it first.
A football goal: the mouth faces -z by default, the net runs d back along +z.
A net on two posts, w between the post centres and h high at the posts.
A lounger lying along x, l long and h to the mattress top.
A parasol: a pole h tall under a cone canopy of radius r. add_beach_set puts each lounger and each parasol on the ground under itself.
